reasoning: Spot identification: Flop decision, hero SB OOP, 3 villains active (UTG opener c-betting, CO flat, BTN flat, BB folded). On J-high two-tone diamond, UTG c-bets at 25% as a near-range bet — value (JJ+, KK, AA, AJ, QQ-AA overpairs, sets 55/JJ rare), draws (AdKd, AdQd-blocked-by-Ad-hero-no, KdQd, suited diamond broadway), and air with backdoor (AK-no-diamond bluffing). Hero's Ad meaningfully removes AdKd/AdQd (the heavy nut-FD combos that UTG bets with). CO flat range 8-10% (88-JJ, AJs-AQs, suited broadway, suited connectors 76s+); on J65dd CO continues with set-J (JJ-rare-flatted), pair-J + diamond (AJs-with-Ad-blocked-by-hero so JJs/QJs/KJs/TJs subset), diamond-FDs (KdQd, KdTd, QdTd, JdTd, suited gappers with diamond), straight-draws (87s, 78s OESD via 4 or 9). CO is range-capped — no AA/KK/AK preflop 3-bet missing. BTN flat range 8-10% similar to CO but slightly wider on suited-connectors and gappers; continues on this wet board with similar bucket — JX-diamond, FDs, OESDs. BTN is also range-capped. Equity/range tensions: Hero's AdQs has TWO clean overcards (6 outs to top pair) plus Ad-nut-FD-blocker. Raw equity vs UTG's c-bet range is ~30-34%; vs combined 3-villain continue range ~25-30%; 4-way realization 0.75 puts effective equity ~19-23%. Pot odds 2.5 to win 15 = 14.3% needed — hero is priced in by raw equity but realization is compromised OOP with 2 capped villains who can raise behind and an SPR ~7 making turn/river OOP playable expensive. The Ad blocker is the load-bearing factor — it removes 3 nut-flush combos from each villain's continue range, which reduces stack-off threat and gives hero implicit overcard-to-top-pair equity that the villains' calling ranges don't crush. Spot-specific factors: Hero is OOP-early (SB) with 2 capped villains LEFT TO ACT behind — squeeze-pressure exists; CO and BTN can raise hero's continue and force a fold-vs-equity decision. Pot-cascade likely collapses to 3-way by turn (one of CO/BTN x-folds). Decision: CALL — pot odds + Ad-blocker + 6 overcard outs justify continuation; RAISE is dominated because hero has no made hand and 2 capped villains behind can flat or 3-bet a check-raise with sets/2pr that crush, while air folds out cheaply; FOLD discards a hand with positive raw equity and a critical nut-FD blocker. The Sonnet 3-1-1 CALL/RAISE/FOLD split is fairly clean — RAISE faction overweighted the Ad-blocker semi-bluff value without crediting the OOP-early position with 2 villains behind (squeeze-pressure suppresses CR-bluff EV); FOLD faction overweighted the no-pair-no-draw frame without crediting Ad-blocker + correct pot odds. Confidence LOW because OOP-early-SB defense with overcards-plus-blocker vs MW-c-bet is a known solver-thin spot between mix-CALL and exploit-FOLD; queue for solver verify.

Spot identification: Preflop decision, hero BTN closing the open + 2 flats action, 3 villains active (UTG opener, HJ flat, CO flat). Hero Ad9c (offsuit weak Ace, position-favored holding). Facing 2.5bb to call, pot 9bb (UTG 2.5 + HJ 2.5 + CO 2.5 + SB 0.5 + BB 1 — but pot reported 9bb confirms blinds included). Pot odds 2.5 to win 11.5 = 17.9%. Per-villain range chains: UTG opens 2.5bb with standard tight 14% range (TT+, AJs+, AKo, KQs, suited broadway 98s+, suited connectors 87s+). HJ flatted UTG with range 5-8% (88-JJ, AJs-AQs, suited broadway KQs/KJs/QJs, suited connectors 76s-T9s); HJ is range-CAPPED — no AA/KK/AK that would 3-bet vs UTG. CO flatted UTG + HJ with similar 6-8% range slightly wider on suited connectors and gappers (overcalling structure invites more speculative hands); CO is also range-capped. The two flats compress the pot equity heavily — each villain has a value-skewed broadway/pair range that dominates A9o's playability postflop. Equity/range tensions: A9o vs the combined UTG-open + HJ-flat + CO-flat range has raw equity ~22-26% (vs 3 villains in a non-all-in cold-call scenario this is moot — what matters is realization and postflop playability). 4-way realization 0.75 puts effective postflop equity ~16-19%. Pot odds need 17.9%. A9o is RIGHT AT the marginal threshold. The structural concerns: (1) A9o is REVERSE-DOMINATED by UTG's AJ/AQ/AK and HJ/CO's AJs/AQs — when hero flops an Ace, hero is often crushed; (2) 9-kicker is weak — pairing the 9 against 3 villains' overpair-heavy continuing ranges rarely wins at showdown; (3) postflop multi-way realization with offsuit weak Ace is poor — no backdoor flush, only backdoor straight via 78T or similar narrow runners. Spot-specific factors: Hero is IP-closing (BTN behind 3 villains; SB and BB still to act behind — squeeze risk from blinds is moderate but typically blinds defend wide not squeeze A9o-pressuring hands). Closing-action is a positive (realization advantage IP); the two flats are net-positive for hero's pot odds but net-negative for hero's hand class because dominated-Ace + weak-kicker scales poorly in MW. Pot-cascade: 4-way pots collapse to 2-3 way by river; A9o postflop maneuverability is limited. Decision: CALL — pot odds 17.9% needed vs ~16-19% effective realized equity is a coin-flip-thin call, but IP-closing position + the implicit equity from rare-but-real flops (A9x two-pair, 99x set-9, 987/A98 connected boards) plus blocker value (As removes AA/AK combos from villain ranges) tilts marginally to CALL. Adjacent FOLD is highly mixable here — the GTO frequency is probably FOLD 55-65% / CALL 35-45% given the dominated-Ace MW realization tax. RAISE (squeeze) is poor because hero's range is too pot-committed by 4 active villains to credibly polarize, and A9o is not a value-squeeze hand. Sonnet 3-2 FOLD/CALL split — FOLD faction correctly weighted the reverse-domination + weak-kicker MW realization tax; CALL faction weighted the raw pot odds + closing position. Confidence LOW because A9o BTN cold-call vs UTG+2-flats is at the GTO marginal threshold (mix-frequency spot); queue for solver verify — could easily be a 60-FOLD/40-CALL mix where the modal action is FOLD.

Spot-specific factors: Hero is OOP-middle (MP, with 2 villains CO+BTN LEFT TO ACT BEHIND and UTG already checked indicating range-capped weakness OR slowplay strength) — donk-leading from MP on this texture is dominated because (1) hero's MP-flat range is range-capped (no AA/KK/AK 3-bet missing), so a lead announces hero is unbalanced; (2) CO/BTN behind can raise wide with their dense made-straight/set/FD continuing ranges; (3) UTG's check is range-balanced (mix of give-up and slowplay) — a lead gets called or raised by the slowplay portion crushing 9-4.
